relations.note: Ahura Mazda creates Tishtrya and appoints him overseer of the stars.

relations.myth: Empowerment before the second Apaosha combat
relations.note: Ahura Mazda sacrifices to Tishtrya and grants him overwhelming accumulated strength.

relations.myth: White and black horses battle over rain
relations.note: Apaosha first defeats Tishtrya, but the empowered Tishtrya wins their rematch.

relations.myth: Distribution of waters across the seven regions
relations.note: Satavaesa follows Tishtrya-raised waters and directs them toward the seven regions.

relations.myth: Tishtrya receives the seed of waters
relations.note: Tishtrya receives the brightness or seed of the waters from Apąm Napāt.

relations.myth: Distribution of rain among the lands
relations.note: Apąm Napāt helps distribute the waters raised through Tishtrya's rain-making work.

relations.myth: Path opened for the arrow-like celestial flight
relations.note: Mithra opens or indicates the broad road for Tishtrya's arrow-like flight.

relations.myth: Divine powers aid the celestial course
relations.note: The Amesha Spentas authorize Tishtrya's course and assist the associated arrow's passage.

relations.myth: Good Reward follows the celestial arrow
relations.note: Aši Vaŋuhī follows behind during the arrow-like journey associated with Tishtrya.

relations.myth: Parendi accompanies the celestial arrow
relations.note: Parendi follows the arrow's journey on a light chariot beside Aši.

relations.myth: Rain-clouds follow Haoma's world-increasing paths
relations.note: Clouds raised through Tishtrya's work travel along paths previously traversed by Haoma.

relations.myth: Wind carries Tishtrya's rain-clouds
relations.note: Wind moves vapor and clouds after Tishtrya raises water from Vourukaša.

relations.myth: Distribution of rain among the lands
relations.note: Watery Glory joins the divine beings distributing waters raised by Tishtrya.

relations.myth: Distribution of rain among the lands
relations.note: The righteous Fravašis assist the distribution of waters produced through Tishtrya's work.

relations.myth: Hostile pairikās obstruct the water-bearing stars
relations.note: Tishtrya opposes Angra Mainyu's attack by dispersing the pairikās he sends.

relations.myth: Hostile aerial beings attack the water-stars
relations.note: Tishtrya drives the airborne pairikās away from the cosmic sea.

relations.myth: Binding of the disastrous year
relations.note: Tishtrya restrains the female pairikā Dužyāiryā with double and triple bonds.

relations.myth: Drought demons obstruct the primordial rain
relations.note: Spenjagr aids Apōš during Tishtrya's rain battle, though Tishtrya does not strike him.

relations.myth: Lightning defeats Spenjagr during the rain battle
relations.note: Ādur Wāzišt strikes Spenjagr while Tishtrya combats the other rain-blocking forces.
Some Middle Persian passages equate Tīr with Tištar despite contradictory astronomical traditions.

relations.myth: Proposed divine pair at Dzhartepa II
relations.note: A contested interpretation identifies the mural's divine pair as Nana and Tishtrya.

relations.myth: Tishtrya's flight compared with the archer's arrow
relations.note: Tishtrya's swift celestial movement is compared to Ǝrəxša's supernaturally aided arrow.
